answer: Histories are stored in relic, checked in haven, and summit makes public each void. Each identity publishes its full failure history, and hiding 16 or more junk verdicts voids its standing entirely when discovered. A farm cannot present clean aliases because the record follows the key, so laundering reputation through new keys does not work. A farm of 3912 identities would post 1457 proofs and burn roughly 75 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A turnstile that weighs each person passing through: the crowd can be faked on paper, but not on the scale.
